conditionCards.sugar1: Try to keep meal timing steady instead of eating heavily at random times.
conditionCards.sugar2: Pair rice or carbs with vegetables or protein so energy release feels slower.
conditionCards.sugar3: Use your sugar readings and symptoms to decide when a real doctor review is needed.
conditionCards.bp1: Lower-salt meals and a calmer evening routine are often more realistic than sudden strict dieting.
conditionCards.bp2: Short walks, hydration, and better sleep usually support BP better than one intense exercise day.
conditionCards.bp3: If readings stay high or symptoms feel new, review this with a doctor instead of relying only on the plan.
conditionCards.sleep1: Aim for a repeatable sleep window first, even before trying to sleep much longer.
conditionCards.sleep2: Reduce heavy meals, caffeine, and bright-screen time late at night.
conditionCards.sleep3: If poor sleep comes with anxiety, snoring, or exhaustion, discuss it with a clinician.
conditionCards.movement1: Use small daily movement blocks you can repeat, not rare high-effort exercise bursts.
conditionCards.movement2: Anchor walking or stretching right after meals or after waking up.
conditionCards.movement3: Track consistency first. Weight or stamina usually improves after the routine becomes stable.
